# Attribution

<!-- Written by `npm run world -- attribution` from world/manifest.yaml and the sources the records cite. Do not edit by hand. -->

WikiWorldModel's own code is under the Apache License 2.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)), and its records and
documentation are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 ([LICENSE-DATA](LICENSE-DATA)). It is
built on the work of others, credited here. Anything that shows the world, or is made from it, credits
them in the same way: the viewer does, under *Data and licences*.

## Datasets

The build reads these datasets, each pinned by its checksum in [world/manifest.yaml](world/manifest.yaml),
under the licence given. A build may read only CC0, CC BY and public-domain data.

### Data for Figure 2.4a of IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 2: CO₂, methane and N₂O from ice cores, the last 800 kyr

Ahn, J. (2023). Chapter 2 of the Working Group I Contribution to the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report - data for Figure 2.4 (v20221219). NERC EDS Centre for Environmental Data Analysis, 3 July 2023. Its CO₂ is from Bereiter et al. (2015), Geophysical Research Letters 42, 542–549, doi:10.1002/2014GL061957, and its methane from Loulergue et al. (2008), Nature 453, 383–386, doi:10.1038/nature06950.

- Licence: CC-BY-4.0. The CEDA catalogue record, the archive's 00README_catalogue_and_licence.txt and the DOI's DataCite record all state CC BY 4.0. Its License.txt adds that users should also cite the publications the data come from. Read here instead of the same composites at NOAA NCEI (studies 17975 and 6093), whose records ask for a citation and state no licence (the DOIs' rights lists are empty), and whose contributors are not US government employees, so the files cannot simply be taken for public domain.
- Credit: CO₂ and methane from ice cores (Bereiter et al. 2015; Loulergue et al. 2008), as tabulated for IPCC AR6
- DOI: [10.5285/60eeb3cce51a457cb5ee1c577a0c8674](https://doi.org/10.5285/60eeb3cce51a457cb5ee1c577a0c8674)
- From: <https://catalogue.ceda.ac.uk/uuid/60eeb3cce51a457cb5ee1c577a0c8674>
- Source id: `src:ar6-wg1-fig2-4`

from them as data; the quotes stay under the terms given.
